//:
Every literal the token sweep left behind, and nothing else.

This is a ratchet, not an exemption list. scripts/css-token-sweep.test.mjs
compares it against the tree with a set equality, so a literal that is not
recorded here fails the build and a recorded literal that has been migrated
fails it too. Adding a row is therefore a deliberate act with a reviewer,
which is the only property that makes a debt list shrink instead of drift.

Rows are grouped by file and property and hold the declaration value, not a
line number: two rules that paint the same literal share one row, and
editing anything above a rule does not churn the ledger.

The colour half is empty. Phase 5 gave the last 245 colour literals a role:
the four --status-*-edge borders, --status-progress, the six --syntax-*
inks, --accent-inverse, --fg-inverse-muted and the two --chrome-fg-* steps
absorbed the opaque ones, and every translucent one became a color-mix()
over a tier-2 token, which is what an alpha needs and what no primitive
could hold. `npm run lint:css` now fails on a hex or an rgb() outside
app/styles/tokens-*.css, so this half of the ledger cannot refill quietly.

What is left of the scale half is the set docs/theming.md says stays
literal, and the lint agrees with it declaration for declaration:
`border-radius: 50%` means a circle rather than a step; a box-shadow's
offsets and blur are a geometry the size ladder makes no claim about, and
the sweep records each length and ink of a composed ring separately; and a
single-digit z-index orders an element inside a stacking context its parent
already opened, which is not a page layer.
